paragraphs:
Thomas Jefferson University is a private research university in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Established in 1824, the University officially combined with Philadelphia University in 2017. Around 242 of the student population are international students from different countries.

The University is an internationally-recognized academic medical center known for providing architecture, business, design, engineering, fashion & textiles, health, science, and social science courses.

What is the Thomas Jefferson University acceptance rate for International Students?

The Thomas Jefferson University acceptance rate is 63%.

There are lots of academic facilities across the campuses in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. From the Jefferson Hospitals for Neuroscience, Advanced Care, and Orthopedics to the Marcus Institute of Integrative Health and beyond, the University has earned its reputation for academic excellence via first-rate facilities. There are also several libraries and classrooms across its campuses.

The Scott Memorial Library is the main library on campus, with a range of online and print resources in addition to study spaces. The Kanbar Campus Center provides fitness facilities such as cardio and strength training equipment, group classes, and personal training to students. There are also multiple dining options on campus, including cafes, coffee shops, and food courts.

Student Life

Thomas Jefferson University provides its students with a rich and varied campus life via the hundreds of student clubs at the institution. There is something for everyone, from volunteer groups to athletic teams and beyond. Cultural festivals are held on campus to integrate students and complement the many events and concerts students can see. There are 18 varsity sports teams at Thomas Jefferson University, a fitness center, and intramural sports programs for active students to enjoy during their time at University. The Office of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion supports international students and promotes diversity across campus.
